definition_title: Cost-bounded ideals generated by iterated derivatives
natural_language_statement: A word of derivation indices acts recursively: for a nonempty word i :: rest, its value on f is D i applied to the value for rest; the cost is the sum of the assigned real costs. derivativeIdeal D cost bound f is the ideal spanned by all such word derivatives whose cost is at most bound. The bundle also defines derivativeCore I as the elements of I whose image under a derivation remains in I, and proves membership results for bounded-cost derivatives and for f itself when the bound is nonnegative.
explanation: These definitions organize iterated derivatives by a real-valued cost budget. The membership lemmas place each admissible word derivative, and the empty-word value f, in the generated ideal; derivativeCore captures stability under one derivation.
